book_title: The Second Epistle of Peter the Apostle.

verses.text: <sc>SIMON PETER</sc> seruant and Apostle of <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ, to them that haue obtained equal faith vvith vs in the iustice of our God and Sauiour <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ.
Grace to you and peace be accomplished in the knovvledge of God and Christ <sc>IESVS</sc> our Lord:
as al things of his diuine povver vvhich pertaine to life and godlines, are giuen vs by the knovvledge of him vvhich hath called vs by his ovvne propre glorie and vertue,
by vvhom he hath giuen vs most great and pretious promises: that by these you may be made partakers of the diuine nature, fleeing the corruption of that concupiscence vvhich is in the vvorld.
And you employing al care, minister ye in your faith, vertue: and in vertue, knovvledge:
and in knovvledge, abstinence: and in abstinence, patience: and in patience, pietie:
and in pietie, loue of the fraternitie: and in the loue of the fraternitie, charitie.
For if these things be present vvith you, & abound: they shal make you not vacant, nor vvithout fruite in the knovvledge of our Lord <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ.
For he that hath not these things ready, is blinde, and groping vvith his hand, hauing forgotten the purging of his old sinnes.
VVherfore, brethren, labour the more that by good vvorkes you may make sure your vocation and election. for, doing these things, you shal not sinne at any time.
For so there shal be ministred to you aboundantly an entrance into the euerlasting kingdom of our Lord and Sauiour <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ.
For the vvhich cause I vvil begin to admonish you alvvaies of these things: and you in deede knovving & being confirmed in the present truth.
But I thinke it meete as long as I am in this tabernacle, to stirre you vp by admonition:
being certaine that the laying avvay of my tabernacle is at hand, according as our Lord <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ also signified to me.
And I vvil doe my diligence, you to haue often after my decease also, that you may keepe a memorie of these things.

<na>[1]</na> For not hauing folovved vnlearned fables, haue vve made the povver and <na>[2]</na> <alt>`presence</alt>' of our Lord <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ knovven to you: but <na>[3]</na> cmade beholders of his greatenesse.

notes.text: The Epistle in the Transfiguration of our Lord, Aug. 6.

verses.text: For, [1] he receiuing from God his father honour and glorie, this maner of voice comming dovvne to him from the magnifical glorie, This is my beloued sonne in vvhom I haue pleased my self, heare him.
And this voice vve heard brought from heauen, vvhen vve vvere vvith him in the <na>[1]</na> holy mounte.

notes.text: holy mount. You see that places are made holy by Christ's presence, and that all places be not alike holy. See Annot. Act. 7, 33.

verses.text: And vve haue the prophetical vvord more sure: vvhich you doe vvel attending vnto, as to a candel shining in a darke place, vntil the day davvne, and the day starre arise in your hartes: ⊢
vnderstanding this first that no prophecie of scripture is made by priuate interpretation.
For, <cr>[1]</cr> not by mans vvil vvas prophecie brought at any time: but the holy men of God spake, inspired vvith the holy Ghost.

chapters.summary: Hovv much God hath done for them, making them Christians : 5 and that they againe must doe their part, not hauing onely faith, but al other vertues also and good vvorkes, that so they may haue the more assurance to enter into the kingdom of heauen. 13 And that he is so careful to admonish them, knovving that his death is at hand, knovving also most certainly the comming of Christ by the vvitnes of the Father him self, as also by the Prophets. Concerning vvhom he vvarneth them that they folovv not priuate spirites, but the holy Ghost ( speaking novv in the Church. )

verses.text: <sc>BVT</sc> there vvere also false-prophets in the people, as also in you there <cr>[1]</cr> shal be lying maisters vvhich shal bring in sectes of perdition, and denie him that hath bought them, <na>[2]</na> cthe Lord: bringing vpon them selues speedie perdition.
And <na>[1]</na> many shal folovv their riotousnesses, by vvhom the vvay of truth shal be blasphemed.

notes.text: Heretikes ( of vvhom he prophecieth here ) do gaine scholers, by preaching libertie, and by their ovvne licentious life ; vvhich is specially ioyned to the heresie of these daies.

verses.text: and in auarice shal they <na>[1]</na> cvvith feined vvordes make merchandise of you. vnto vvhom the iudgement novv long since ceaseth not: and their perdition slumbereth not.

notes.text: Al the svveete vvordes of heretikes, speaking much of the vvord of the Lord, the Gospel, IESVS CHRIST &c. are but termes of art to bie and sel poore mens soules.

verses.text: For if God spared not Angels sinning: but vvith the ropes of Hel being dravven dovvne into Hel deliuered them to be tormented, that they should be reserued vnto iudgement:
& he spared not the original vvorld, but <cr>[1]</cr> kept the eight, Noë, the preacher of iustice, bringing in the deluge vpon the vvorld of the impious.
And <cr>[1]</cr> bringing the cities of the Sodomites and of the Gomorrheites into ashes, he damned them vvith subuersion, putting an example of them that shal doe impiously:
and <cr>[1]</cr> deliuered iust Lot oppressed by the iniurie and luxurious conuersation of the abominable men.
for in sight and <na>[1]</na> hearing he vvas iust: dvvelling vvith them vvho from day to day vexed the iust soule vvith vniust vvorkes.
Our Lord knovveth to deliuer the godly from tentation, but to reserue the vniust vnto the day of iudgement to be tormented:
<na>[1]</na> and especially them vvhich vvalke after the flesh in concupiscence of vncleannesse, and contemne dominion, bold, self-pleasers: they feare not to bring in sectes, blaspheming.
Vvhereas Angels being greater in strength and povver, beare not the execrable iudgement <na>[1]</na> against them.
But these men as vnreasonable beastes, naturally tending to the snare and into destruction, <na>[1]</na> in those things vvhich they knovv not, blaspheming, shal perish in their corruption,

notes.text: So heretikes blaspheme the highest mysteries of our faith through ignorance.

verses.text: receiuing the revvard of iniustice, esteeming for a pleasure the delightes of a day: <na>[1]</na> bcoinquinations and spottes, flovving in delicacies, in their feastings rioting vvith you,
hauing eies ful of adulterie and incessant sinne: alluring vnstable soules, hauing their hart exercised vvith auarice, the children of malediction:
leauing the right vvay they haue erred, hauing folovved the vvay of Balaam of Bosor, vvhich loued the revvard of iniquitie,
but <cr>[1]</cr> had a checke of his madnesse. the dumme beast vnder the yoke, speaking vvith mans voice, prohibited the folishnes of the prophet.
These are fountaines vvithout vvater, and cloudes, tossed vvith vvhirlevvindes, to vvhom the mist of darkenesse is reserued.
For, speaking the proud things of vanitie, they allure in the desires of fleshly riotousnes, those that escape a litle, vvhich conuerse in errour,
<cr>[1]</cr> promising them libertie, vvhereas them selues are the slaues of corruption. for, <na>[2]</na> vvherevvith a man is ouercome: of that he is the slaue also.

notes.text: Vvho euer promised more libertie to their folovvers then Luther, Caluin, & the like, taking avvay penance, fasting, continencie or chastitie, keeping of vovves, necessitie of good vvorkes ( because faith doeth al ) obedience to Ecclesiastical pastors and Coūcels, and such like? · Io. 8, 34. Ro. 6, 16.

verses.text: For if fleeing from the coinquinations of the vvorld in the knovvledge of our Lord and Sauiour <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ, they againe intangled vvith the same be ouercome: <cr>[1]</cr> the later things are become vnto them vvorse then the former.
For it vvas better for them not to knovv the vvay of iustice, then after the knovvledge, to turne backe from that holy commandement vvhich vvas deliuered to them.
For, that of the true prouerbe is chaunced to them, <cr>[1]</cr> The dogge returned to his vomite: and, The sovve vvashed <na>[2]</na> cinto her vvallovving in the mire.

chapters.summary: As not onely Prophets, but also false-prophets vvere in the old Testament, so novv likevvise there shal be Maisters of Heresie, to the damnation of them selues, and of their folovvers. 4 And of their damnation he pronounceth by examples ( as he comforteth the vertuous Catholikes or true beleeuers vvith the example of Lot ) because of their railing at their Superiors and Prelates, their blaspheming of Catholike doctrine, their voluptuous liuing, their lecherie, their couetousnes, their maner of seducing, and the persons seduced, 20 for vvhom it had been lesse damnable, if they had neuer been Christians.

verses.text: <sc>THIS</sc> loe the second epistle I vvrite to you my deerest, <na>[1]</na> cin vvhich I stirre vp by admonition your sincere minde:
that you may be mindeful of those vvordes vvhich I told you before from the holy Prophetes, and of your Apostles, of the preceptes of our Lord and Sauiour.
Knovving this first, that <cr>[1]</cr> in the last daies shal come mockers in deceit, vvalking according to their ovvne concupiscences,
saying, Vvhere is his promise or his comming? For since the time that the fathers slept, al things do so perseuere from the beginning of creature.
for they are vvilfully ignorant of this, that the heauens vvere before, & the earth, out of vvater, and through vvater, consisting by the vvord of God:
by the vvhich, that vvorld then, being ouerflovved vvith vvater perished.
But the heauens vvhich novv are, & the earth, are by the same vvord kept in store, reserued to fire vnto the day of iudgement & of the perdition of the impious men.
But this one thing be not ignorant of, my deerest, that <cr>[1]</cr> one day vvith our Lord is as a thousand yeres, & a thousand yeres as one day.
Our Lord slacketh not his promis, as some do esteeme it: but he doth patiently for you, <cr>[1]</cr> not vvilling that any perish, but that al returne to penance.

And <cr>[1]</cr> the day of our Lord shal come as a theefe in the vvhich the heauens shal passe vvith great violence, but the elementes shal be resolued vvith heate, and the earth and the vvorkes vvhich are in it, shal be burnt.
Therfore vvhereas al these thinges are to be dissolued: vvhat maner of men ought you to be in holy conuersations and godlinesse,
expecting and hasting vnto the comming of the day of our Lord, by vvhich the heauens burning shal be resolued, and the elementes shal melt vvith the heate of fire?
But vve expect <cr>[1]</cr> nevv heauens and a nevv earth according to his promises, in vvhich iustice inhabiteth.
For the vvhich cause my deerest, expecting these things, labour earnestly to be found immaculate and vnspotted to him in peace:
and <cr>[1]</cr> the longanimitie of our Lord, do ye account saluation, as also our most deere brother Paul according to the vvisedom giuen him hath vvritten to you:

as also in al epistles, speaking in them of these things, in the vvhich are certaine things hard to be vnderstoode, vvhich the vnlearned and vnstable depraue, as also the rest of the Scriptures, to their ovvne perdition.
You therefore brethren, foreknovving, take heede lest ledde aside by the errour of the vnvvise you fal avvay from your ovvne stedfastnes.
but grovv in grace and in knovvledge of our Lord and sauiour <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ. To him be glorie both novv and vnto the day of eternitie. Amen.

chapters.summary: These tvvo Epistles he vvriteth to confirme them in the Apostles doctrine, and vvarneth them of scorners that shal come, and denie Domesday. 5 Whose vaine argument he ansvvereth, and giueth the reason of Gods so long patience, 10 exhorting to al holines of life in respect of that terrible day. 16 Finally giuing vvarning of such as misinterprete S. Paules Epistles & the other Scriptures, and that vve must not for any thing fall from the true faith.
